posts.preview: Today, we took time to visit Nakara Factory, a Namibian tannery and leather manufacturing company in Windhoek, established in 1980. The company tans and processes bovine, game, Swakara and other leather, and manufactures garments, bags, accessories, upholstery and other leather products for local, sub-regional, regi...
Nakara employs 160 workers and is one of the few companies transforming raw materials such as animal skins and hides into finished products ready for the market

Our leather industry remains very small and needs urgent government attention to maximise its potential and create more decent jobs throughout the entire supply value chain—from the cow skin to the finished product

The industry is unique and exotic, with significant potential to explore new markets. Furniture and woodworking businesses can add leather to their products, while shoe manufacturers can connect with Nakara for locally produced leather materials
